### **1. Core AI/ML Engineering Fundamentals**

Three things were still open, and when I clicked it, the minute I clicked it, I am able to go and view it. That is the basic concept of cache." [30 July 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan]
    *   **Why emphasized:** These are fundamental concepts that AI engineers will encounter frequently, especially in interviews, and are crucial for optimizing performance and cost. Caching solves problems related to latency, recompute, and cost. [31 July 2026, Page 11-12 — Siddharth Saminathan]

*   **Prompt Engineering Techniques:** Siddharth explained different ways to engineer prompts, including JSON-based/structured output prompting and few-shot/one-shot prompting. He likened an LLM to a "newborn baby" that needs to be taught what to do.

He also stressed the importance of making "your own prompt" rather than relying solely on AI-generated ones. [28 July 2026, Page 27-28 — Siddharth Saminathan]

### **2. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and Retrieval Strategies**
*   **RAG Architecture and Implementation:** Siddharth guided trainees on implementing RAG systems, focusing on the need for comprehensive and high-quality information retrieval, not just relevant information.
    *   "For this, you can, you need to fix your retrieval because right now your retrieval is only giving relevant information. I want completeness on information, okay? I want quality and completeness, not just quality, okay?" [22 July 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan]
    *   He instructed trainees to study RAG and apply it to their projects. [27 July 2026, Page 1-3 — Siddharth Saminathan]
    *   **Why emphasized:** To ensure the AI system provides exhaustive and high-quality reports, which requires robust retrieval mechanisms.

*   **Re-ranking Strategies:** Siddharth advised against solely relying on LLM-based re-rankers and encouraged trainees to develop their own retrieval and re-ranking strategies tailored to their specific documents and training transcripts.
    *   "LLM-based re-ranker and all anybody can do that. You don't need training for that. OK, we will need to come up with our own retrieval strategy and re-ranking strategy.     *   He also guided on understanding the difference between using and not using the Scroll API for document retrieval. [27 July 2026, Page 1-3 — Siddharth Saminathan]
